questions.subject: english
questions.prompt: In one story, a tiny mouse beats a big lion by being clever. In another, a small girl outwits a bully. Which idea turns up in both stories?
choices: Being clever can matter more than being big
questions.explanation: In both stories the smaller character wins by using their brain, not their strength.

questions.subject: english
questions.prompt: Mia is lonely until a stray dog follows her home. Sam starts a new school and meets a mate at lunch. A young joey finds a new mob. What idea do all three stories share?
questions.explanation: Each character starts out alone and ends up with someone or somewhere they belong.

questions.subject: english
questions.prompt: Two brothers argue over a cricket bat, then team up to beat the big kids. Two neighbours fight over a fence, then work together in a bushfire. What relationship idea is repeated?
choices: Older people are wiser than children
Rivals can become friends when they face a shared problem
questions.explanation: In both stories, people who were fighting join forces to deal with a bigger problem.

questions.subject: english
questions.prompt: A story begins: "Long ago, in a dry red valley, a lone emu searched for water." What does this opening do for the reader?
choices: It sets up the time, place and main character
questions.explanation: The opening tells us when, where and who the story is about.

questions.subject: english
questions.prompt: A chapter ends with the words: "Then the old shed door creaked slowly open." Why might the writer end the chapter here?
choices: To show the story is finished
To teach the reader a new word
To make the reader want to read the next chapter
questions.explanation: Stopping at an exciting moment makes the reader curious about what happens next.

questions.subject: english
questions.prompt: Which sentence would a writer use to make a quiet, peaceful moment feel slow and calm?
choices: The long golden afternoon drifted by as the gum leaves swayed and the creek murmured past.
questions.explanation: A long, flowing sentence with soft words slows the pace and feels calm.

questions.subject: english
questions.prompt: A story is set on an outback farm in a long drought. The dam is almost empty. How does this setting help the plot?
choices: It gives the characters a real problem to solve
It shows the characters are rich
It tells us the story is a poem
questions.explanation: The drought creates the problem, finding water, which drives what the characters do.

questions.subject: english
questions.prompt: A writer says: "Jack's hands shook and he stared at his shoes." What does this show about Jack?
questions.explanation: Shaking hands and not looking up are signs of feeling nervous.

questions.subject: english
questions.prompt: In a plot, what is the climax?
choices: The part that introduces the characters
The most exciting moment, when the problem reaches its peak
The last sentence of the story
questions.explanation: The climax is the high point, where the main problem is at its biggest and most tense.

questions.subject: english
questions.prompt: Read this line: "The breeze whispered in the gum trees." Which word play is the writer using?
questions.explanation: A breeze cannot really whisper. Giving it a human action is personification.

questions.subject: english
choices: The cat sat on the mat.
She ran as fast as a cheetah.
questions.explanation: Alliteration repeats the same first sound. Here it is the s sound in slippery, snakes, slid, silently and south.

questions.subject: english
questions.prompt: A poet writes: "The classroom was a zoo." Which device is this?
questions.explanation: It says one thing is another without using like or as. That is a metaphor, not a simile.
